title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
content_c:
Klopp wants Germany football team to 'reclaim the flag'
September 17, 2026
Jürgen Klopp used his first squad announcement as Germany's new head coach to deliver a stirring speech in favor of what he described as "positive patriotism."
"I'd like to reclaim the flag for myself — or for us," Klopp said.
"I want us to always wave it in a way that makes no one think: 'What's wrong with you?'" he said. "But, rather, that people simply get the feeling that you're happy and understand how lucky you are to have been born, raised or moved to this wonderful country."
This was an apparent reference to the recent state election in Saxony-Anhalt, which the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) won in a landslide victory.
Klopp said of the election "that some people probably thought it was OK, while many others thought: 'Good heavens, what's going on there?"
The former Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool head coach was quick to say he is not a political expert and that he doesn't want to talk about politics at every press conference, but that he doesn't want to "leave national pride to the wrong people."
Rather than leaving that up to misinterpretation, something Klopp said was possible, he turned toward the concept of "positive patriotism."
"I can be proud to be German and still be open-minded, diverse, kind and friendly," he said. "I actually think we're a wonderful country."
The 59-year-old added that, just as he had selected the current squad by looking at what the country had to offer in terms of football talent rather than what it was lacking, it might help to do the same when looking at the country as a whole.
This echoed a similar sentiment of former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann, who spoke emotionally after Germany's Euro 2024 exit.
"Being together must become more important again. We must not be consumed with envy, always paint everything in a negative light and not begrudge our neighbors anything," Nagelsmann said.
"I believe that if everyone starts within their own small circle — on their street, helping their neighbors when something comes up [...] [we can] support one another, integrate everyone, welcome them, and help them feel at home, and bring people together to work with us toward a better future."
Klopp highlights power of football
Klopp was quick to turn to the power of football, while also recognizing its place in wider society.
"It's more important that we have doctors. It's more important that we have nurses. It's more important that we have a great, great many people in a wide variety of professions," he said, before adding that football can "foster a sense of community that lets us truly feel the power of sports."
Klopp cited the recent successes of Alexander Zverev, the world champion field hockey team, the home World Cup in women's basketball and the success of athletes at this summer's European Athletics Championships as further positive examples of the power of sport.
"That's our mission. We have to create the right atmosphere — I know that. But to do that, we need people who are willing to embrace it," he said.
Master class in communication
Klopp's delivery was a textbook example of how to create alignment across his messaging. His squad, made up of 44 players including 11 new faces, is a reflection of the diverse society that Klopp proudly referenced.
His engagement with the media was also strategically smart. After laying down clear boundaries in his first press conference that included him saying he would quit if coverage strayed into the personal, Klopp this time opted to seek to include the media as part of the process while also subtly reminding them of what he sees as their role.
When explaining his choice to name such a large squad with so many new and young players, Klopp said he wasn't going to tell members of the media how to do their job when it comes to assessing players, but said that he knew how he would do it. In between the lines, this was an indirect appeal to the media to choose coverage that would foster the development of this new era of players rather than hinder it by being overly critical or negative.
On top of that, Klopp did all of this while wearing a baseball cap with the words "one of 83 million" written on the front. This is in reference to a Germany's approximate population and an expression about how everyone has an opinion on the Germany team and so is therefore a "Bundestrainer" (national team coach). It also came across as an attempt to assign a shared responsibility for the team's success.
Germany's Euro 2024 campaign briefly instilled some pride over the flag again, as did Germany's women in the Euro 2022 final. The most impactful though, was the 2006 World Cup in Germany, which provided the biggest positive cultural shift in the general German attitude toward national pride since World War II.
Now, through the vehicle of football, Germany's new head coach has declared a desire to restore that pride. Klopp said his whole career had brought him to this moment.
After these words, it felt like all the disappointments the Germany team — and their fans — have endured over the last few years may also have brought them to the right leader.
Edited by: Chuck Penfold
description: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

title: U21-Nationalmannschaft: Paris Brunner und sechs weitere Debütanten im neuen Kader
content_c:
Nach Klopp-Lob Paris Brunner und sechs weitere Debütanten – das ist der neue U21-Kader
Mit sieben Debütanten geht U21-Nationaltrainer Antonio Di Salvo in die kommenden Länderspiele. Paris Brunner (AS Monaco), Wael Mohya (Borussia Mönchengladbach), Francis Onyeka (SV Elversberg), Noahkai Banks (FC Augsburg), Laurin Ulrich (SC Paderborn), Louey Ben Farhat (Karlsruher SC) und Frank Feller (1. FC Heidenheim) sind erstmals dabei.
Einige Neulinge erhalten auch wegen des großen Aufgebots von Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp nun ihre Chance. Klopp hatte am Donnerstag 44 Spieler in zwei Kadern für die kommenden Partien in der Nations League nominiert . Darunter sind mehrere U21-Akteure.
Klopp hatte bereits am Donnerstag die verbliebenen U21-Spieler gelobt. »Morgen wird der U21-Kader bekannt gegeben, und da sind auch ganz viele großartige Jungs dabei«, hatte er bei der Präsentation der 44 Spieler für die A-Nationalmannschaft gesagt. Deshalb wurde die aktuelle Nominierung mit mehr Interesse als üblich verfolgt: Auch sehr junge, unerfahrene Spieler können unter Klopp offenbar leicht ins A-Team rücken.
Tom Bischof vom FC Bayern München hat eine besondere Rolle. Der 21 Jahre alte Mittelfeldspieler ist zunächst Teil des U21-Kaders. Für die Länderspiele des Klopp-Teams gegen Serbien (1. Oktober) und in Griechenland (4. Oktober) reist er dann zur A-Nationalmannschaft.
Gegen Brunner wird ermittelt
Interessant ist auch die Personalie Brunner. Der hochtalentierte Nachwuchsspieler hatte seinen Ausgleichstreffer im französischen Ligaspiel bei Racing Straßburg (1:1) vor dem gegnerischen Fanblock bejubelt und dabei mit einer Handbewegung ein Messer, das die Kehle durchschneidet, imitiert.
Später sagte Brunner, die Fans hätten »über meine Familie gesprochen, über meine Mutter, über meinen Vater. Ich konnte diejenigen sehen, die mich beschimpft haben.« Er wollte »nicht respektlos sein«, sagte aber, dass seine Geste missverstanden worden sei: »Was ich sagen wollte, war: Was für ein Tor, es ist vorbei.«
Brunner wurde unter anderem bei Borussia Dortmund ausgebildet und galt dort als besonderes, aber auch kompliziertes Talent. Beim BVB wurde er zwischenzeitlich aus »disziplinarischen Gründen« suspendiert, Näheres gab der Club damals nicht bekannt. Später folgte der Wechsel nach Monaco.
Verzichten muss U21-Trainer Di Salvo auf Dennis Seimen (VfB Stuttgart), Nnamdi Collins (Eintracht Frankfurt), Assan Ouédraogo (RB Leipzig), Anton Kade (FC Augsburg), Ilyas Ansah (Hull City) sowie Nelson Weiper (Sturm Graz). Sie sind entweder verletzt oder befinden sich noch im Aufbautraining.
Training, Spiele, Teambuilding – lange Länderspielpause soll genutzt werden
Die U21 spielt in der Qualifikation für die Europameisterschaft 2027 in Serbien und Albanien am 26. September in Riga gegen Lettland. Am 30. September ist Malta auswärts der nächste Gegner. Den Abschluss der EM-Qualifikation bildet das Heimspiel in Bielefeld gegen Georgien (6. Oktober).
»Erstmals haben wir eine so lange Länderspielphase außerhalb eines Turniers. Diese Chance wollen wir mit intensivem Training, erfolgreichen Spielen, abwechslungsreichem Teambuilding und viel Freude am Fußball für uns nutzen«, sagte Di Salvo. »Unser Ziel ist klar: Mit drei Siegen die EM-Qualifikation als Gruppenerster fix machen.«
Di Salvos Mannschaft ist Tabellenführer in Gruppe F. Alle Gruppensieger sowie der beste Gruppenzweite qualifizieren sich direkt für die Endrunde. Die anderen Gruppenzweiten haben über Playoffs noch die Chance zur Turnierteilnahme.
author: DER SPIEGEL
description: Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp versprach »viele großartige Jungs«, nun hat U21-Coach Antonio Di Salvo seinen Kader benannt. Darunter sieben Debütanten – und mit einer Sonderrolle für Bayern-Profi Tom Bischof.

title: Marktbericht: DAX schließt nach US-Zinserhöhung im Plus
content_c:
26.000 Punkte wieder im Blick DAX schließt nach US-Zinserhöhung im Plus
Der DAX hat nach der Zinserhöhung der US-Notenbank zugelegt. Rückenwind kam von fallenden Ölpreisen. Nach Übernahmespekulationen führt der Diagnostikkonzern Qiagen den deutschen Leitindex an.
Der DAX hat am Donnerstag an seine Erholung vom Vortag angeknüpft. Der deutsche Leitindex schloss bei 25.717 Punkten und damit 0,7 Prozent höher als am Vortag. Damit zeigte sich der Aktienmarkt trotz der ersten Zinserhöhung der US-Notenbank Federal Reserve seit 2023 robust. Der deutsche Leitindex hatte schon gestern vor dem US-Zinsentscheid 0,5 Prozent auf 25.538 Punkte zugelegt.
Die Fed hatte am Mittwochabend den Leitzins wie erwartet um 0,25 Prozentpunkte auf eine Spanne von 3,75 bis 4,00 Prozent angehoben. Zugleich signalisierten die Währungshüter, dass im weiteren Jahresverlauf eine zusätzliche Erhöhung möglich ist.
An den europäischen Börsen wurde die Entscheidung zunächst positiv aufgenommen. Marktbeobachter verwiesen darauf, dass die US-Notenbank damit ihre Entschlossenheit im Kampf gegen die Inflation unterstrichen habe. "Die Fed verteidigt ihre Glaubwürdigkeit", kommentierte Michael Heise, Chefökonom von HQ Trust. Er hält eine weitere Zinsanhebung im Oktober oder spätestens Dezember für wahrscheinlich.
Die US-Notenbank Fed reagiere damit "nicht nur auf die hartnäckige Inflation, sondern auch auf gestiegene Zweifel des Anleihemarktes an ihrer Entschlossenheit", kommentierte Volkswirt Johannes Mayr vom Vermögensverwalter Eyb & Wallwitz
Freundlicher Börsenstart in New York
Auch die New Yorker Börsen haben sich am Donnerstag freundlich präsentiert. Der Leitindex Dow Jones der nach der gestrigen US-Zinserhöhung noch deutlich verloren hatte, erholte sich im frühen Handel um 0,5 Prozent. Für den zur Wochenmitte ebenfalls schwächelnden, marktbreiten S&P 500 ging es um 0,9 Prozent hoch. Der technologielastige Nasdaq 100 gewann sogar 1,3 Prozent.
Für Entlastung sorgten an den internationalen Märkten die rückläufigen Ölpreise. Brent und WTI verbilligten sich am Donnerstag zeitweise um mehr als ein Prozent auf etwas über 100 Dollar je Barrel. Beide Sorten hatten bereits am Mittwoch rund drei Dollar verloren.
Berichte vom Mittwoch über alternative Lieferwege für Ölexporte aus Saudi-Arabien dämpften die Sorgen über mögliche Versorgungsengpässe infolge des Konflikts im Nahen Osten. Am Donnerstag hieß es nun in einem Medienbericht, dass China den Iran aufgefordert haben soll, auf eine Eindämmung der Huthi-Rebellen im Jemen hinzuwirken. Diese waren zuletzt für eine Reihe von Angriffen auf Öltanker in der Region verantwortlich, die zur Verknappung des Rohölangebots beitrugen.
Bei den Einzelwerten sorgte Qiagen für Gesprächsstoff. Die Aktien des Diagnostikkonzerns stiegen zeitweise um über fünf Prozent und standen damit an der DAX-Spitze. Auslöser waren neue Übernahmespekulationen. Dem Manager Magazin zufolge interessieren sich neben den bereits genannten Finanzinvestoren KKR, EQT und Advent auch TPG und Bain Capital für das zum Verkauf stehende Unternehmen.
Um Qiagen hatte es in den vergangenen Jahren immer wieder Spekulationen über einen Verkauf oder eine Fusion gegeben. Die Aktie profitiere nun davon, dass das Thema erneut konkret auf den Tisch komme, sagten Händler.
Bilfinger stürzt nach Gewinnwarnung ab
Deutlich schlechter lief es für Bilfinger. Die Aktien des Mannheimer Industriedienstleisters brachen nach einer Senkung der Prognose um mehr als 20 Prozent ein und fielen auf den tiefsten Stand seit rund anderthalb Jahren. Das im MDAX gelistete Unternehmen rechnet wegen der schwächeren Entwicklung im zweiten Halbjahr mit weniger Umsatz und einer deutlich niedrigeren operativen Marge.
Auch Wacker Chemie geriet unter Druck. Die Aktien des Spezialchemiekonzerns verloren rund zwei Prozent. Wacker senkte seine langfristigen Ziele für die operative Umsatzrendite. Statt einer Ebitda-Marge von mehr als 20 Prozent strebt das Unternehmen künftig 13 bis 17 Prozent an. Als Reaktion auf die schwache Chemiekonjunktur und Probleme im Solargeschäft will Wacker zudem seine jährlichen Investitionen auf 300 bis 400 Millionen Euro begrenzen.
Positive Nachrichten kamen derweil aus der deutschen Industrie. Der Auftragsbestand im Verarbeitenden Gewerbe erreichte im Juli ein neues Allzeithoch. Gegenüber dem Vormonat legten die Aufträge um 1,5 Prozent zu, binnen Jahresfrist betrug der Anstieg fast elf Prozent.
Auch die Bank of England beschäftigte die Anleger. Die britische Notenbank beließ ihren Leitzins wie erwartet bei 3,75 Prozent. Die Entscheidung fiel allerdings nur mit sechs zu drei Stimmen. Drei Mitglieder des geldpolitischen Ausschusses plädierten für eine Erhöhung um 0,25 Prozentpunkte.
Notenbankchef Andrew Bailey verwies auf die bislang begrenzten Auswirkungen des Energieschocks auf Preise und Löhne. Je länger die Volatilität anhalte, desto größer würden allerdings die Auswirkungen auf die Inflation und damit auch der Druck auf die Geldpolitik.
author: tagesschau.de
description: Der DAX hat nach der Zinserhöhung der US-Notenbank zugelegt. Rückenwind kam von fallenden Ölpreisen. Nach Übernahmespekulationen führt der Diagnostikkonzern Qiagen den deutschen Leitindex an.

title: Maria Magdalena: Heilige, Sünderin, Liebling der Künste
content_c:
Maria Magdalena: Heilige, Sünderin, Liebling der Künste
16. September 2026
Sie war Apostolin, Prostituierte, Büßerin und Vertraute Jesu, so wurde es seit dem frühen Christentum über Maria Magdalena erzählt. Künstler von Renaissance bis Barock, darunter Tizian, El Greco und Georges de la Tour malten sie im 16. und 17. Jahrhundert als reuige Büßerin, Rembrandt als Zeugin der Auferstehung Christi und Max Beckmann als Vertreter der Neuen Sachlichkeit stellte sie 1917 als Sünderin dar. Knapp hundert Jahre später wurde sie von Lady Gaga in einem Musikvideo verkörpert.
"Maria Magdalena ist wahrscheinlich die facettenreichste und schillerndste Figur der Bibel und auch eine der schillerndsten der europäischen Kulturgeschichte", sagt Bastian Eclercy, Kurator der Ausstellung "Maria Magdalena: Sin. Pray. Love." im Frankfurter Städel Museum. "Sie kommt in der Kunstgeschichte unzählige Male vor."
Was wissen wir über Maria Magdalena?
Aus der Bibel ist nur wenig über Maria Magdalena bekannt, dennoch spielt sie im Neuen Testament eine wichtige Rolle. Die Evangelien berichten, dass Jesus sie von sieben Dämonen befreite, dass sie Jesus begleitete und seine Kreuzigung sowie Grablegung miterlebte. Am Ostermorgen entdeckte sie das leere Grab und wurde zur ersten Zeugin der Auferstehung. Anschließend verkündete sie den Jüngern Jesu die Botschaft vom auferstandenen Christus. "Da wird sie dann als Apostula Apostulorum, also Apostelin der Apostel, bezeichnet", erklärt Bastian Eclercy. "Damit kommt ihr in der Heilsgeschichte eine ganz zentrale Rolle zu."
Doch dabei bleibt es nicht. Um 600 n. Chr. beschädigt Papst Gregor der Große das Bild Maria Magdalenas nachhaltig, indem er sie mit zwei anderen in der Bibel genannten Frauen verschmilzt: mit einer Unbekannten, der im Lukasevangelium genannten Sünderin, die Christus die Füße wäscht, und mit Maria von Bethanien (die ihm ebenfalls die Füße wäscht). Der Papst behauptete, dass die sieben Dämonen, von denen Jesus sie befreit, die sieben Todsünden seien. Damit prägte er maßgeblich Maria Magdalenas Ruf als reuige Prostituierte - was die Bibel in keiner Weise belegt.
Maria Magdalenas Gebeine liegen in Frankreich - angeblich
Im Hochmittelalter kommt dazu noch die Legende auf, Maria Magdalena sei zusammen mit Lazarus und einer Gruppe von Gefährtinnen und Gefährten in einem Boot auf dem Mittelmeer ausgesetzt worden; mit göttlicher Hilfe habe sie die Küste der französischen Provence erreicht, wo sie zunächst missioniert und dann noch rund 30 Jahre in einer Höhle gelebt und Buße getan habe. Noch heute behaupten zwei französische Orte, ihre Gebeine aufzubewahren: Vézelay in Burgund und Saint-Maximin-la-Sainte-Baume in der Provence.
Im 16. Jahrhundert schließlich bewirkten Reformation und Humanismus ein Umdenken und Widerspruch gegen die Verschmelzung der drei Frauen zu einer. Doch erst nach dem Zweiten Vatikanischen Konzil (1962 bis 1965), das tiefgreifende Reformen der römisch-katholischen Liturgie beschloss, wurde die Gleichsetzung Maria Magdalenas mit der anonymen Sünderin offiziell aufgehoben.
"Dieses sehr breite Feld von Rollen, die ihr im Laufe ihrer Geschichte zugeschrieben worden sind, und die in einem gewissen Spannungsverhältnis zueinanderstehen, hat Künstler aller Zeiten und Gattungen offenbar immer wieder in besonderer Weise gereizt und auch herausgefordert," erklärt Bastian Eclercy.
Imagewandel durch das Marienevangelium
Mit der Wiederentdeckung des Marienevangeliums in der Neuzeit wandelte sich das Bild Maria Magdalenas erneut. Die Schrift, die nicht in den biblischen Kanon aufgenommen wurde, zeichnet sie als besonders enge Vertraute Jesu und entfachte eine neue Diskussion über ihre Rolle. Heute gilt sie als eine der einflussreichsten Frauen des frühen Christentums und Schlüsselfigur der feministischen Theologie. "Gerade in den letzten Jahrzehnten wurde sie so zu einer Identifikationsfigur für Frauen, also für weibliche Betrachterinnen, aber eben auch insbesondere für Künstlerinnen der Gegenwart, die die Komponente der selbstbestimmten Frau in ihr sehen", sagt Eclercy.
Lady Gaga verkörperte Maria Magdalena 2011 in ihrem Video zu "Judas" - "der aufregendste künstlerische Moment meiner Karriere", wie sie damals auf Twitter schrieb. Das jüngste Bildnis der Frankfurter Schau, die mehr als 100 Darstellungen der Maria Magdalena zeigt, stammt von der spanischen Künstlerin Nieves González und ist 2025 fertiggestellt worden: "La sfida" (Die Herausforderung) dekonstruiert so ziemlich alle traditionellen Attribute, die Künstler früherer Jahrhunderte Maria Magdalena zugewiesen haben. Wo sie früher büßend gen Himmel blickte, zeigt das Gemälde die Apostolin mit selbstbewusstem Blick auf den Betrachter herabschauend. Wo sonst das Haar lose herabhing und damit auf die sündige Vergangenheit der Trägerin verwies, liegt es hier wie ein Schal sorgfältig gebürstet um ihren Hals. Und wo sonst viel weiße Haut zu sehen war, umhüllt ein dicker roter Daunenmantel ihren Körper. In ihren Händen hält die Jüngerin einen ebenso (blut-)roten Schädel, jahrhundertelang Symbol der Vergänglichkeit - mit dieser Geste klarer Ausdruck ihrer Macht.
Gleichberechtigung hat Maria Magdalena mittlerweile auch offiziell in der katholischen Kirche erfahren: 2016 erhob der damalige Papst Franziskus ihren Gedenktag (22. Juli) in den Rang eines Festes, womit sie in der katholischen Kirche den männlichen Aposteln rechtlich und rituell gleichgestellt ist. Es ist vermutlich nicht das letzte Kapitel ihrer illustren Biografie.
Die Ausstellung "Maria Magdalena: Sin. Pray. Love." ist im Frankfurter Städel Museum bis zum 17.01.2027 zu sehen.
description: Maria Magdalena wurden die unterschiedlichsten Rollen zugeschrieben, kaum etwas davon ist belegt. Eine Frankfurter Schau zeigt, wie die Kunstwelt sie in rund 1000 Jahren immer wieder neu interpretiert hat - bis heute.

title: Henry Zeffman: Andy Burnham and his chancellor have a battle on their hands as the Budget approaches
content_c:
Henry Zeffman: Andy Burnham and his chancellor have a battle on their hands as the Budget approaches
- Published
Today's inflation figures underscore that the economy is the biggest challenge facing Andy Burnham.
It is only 42 days until John Healey's first Budget, and there is increasingly apparent concern at all levels of the government and Labour Party about how that Budget can – or, as it may prove, cannot – substantiate Burnham's rhetoric about offering the biggest change in British politics in 40 years.
Much of the tricky economic environment, yes, is driven by global factors including the persistence, and to some degree worsening, of the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine.
And the AI boom pushing up borrowing costs is another issue affecting many countries.
But there are clearly domestic factors particular to Britain, and on that front it was very striking to hear the former Bank of England chief economist Andy Haldane telling LBC on Tuesday that without signs of cuts to public spending "the markets now suspect that this is a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos".
From somebody who at times has informally advised Burnham's operation, that will sting, not least because a similar criticism has been voiced in recent weeks by the prominent economist Lord O'Neill – another sometime adviser.
The prime minister gave a direct response to Haldane, saying: "That doesn't tell the story. We are not that."
He identified "putting digital ID on hold" as an example of how he had already "taken difficult decisions in this job in relation to reprioritising government spending" and vowed to continue to "take difficult decisions to make sure the economy remains on track".
Digital ID is a striking choice of example. Burnham announced that he was abandoning the scheme in the days before he became prime minister so that he could focus on policies affecting the everyday cost of living.
But the spending was then, within the new government's first few days, re-allocated to cut VAT on household electricity bills.
So in that sense it was not a reduction in public spending, just a reprioritisation. And in any case, the former cabinet minister Darren Jones criticised Burnham at the time on the grounds that the government had not yet allocated the money for digital ID.
Certainly the signs from Healey's first major speech as chancellor last week were that he wants to reassure the markets, promising to "control public spending" and praising Rachel Reeves for beginning to "recover Britain's fiscal discipline".
Burnham and Healey would hardly be the first PM-chancellor double act to adopt different tones and emphasise different priorities in their public appearances.
As a junior minister at the Treasury almost 25 years ago, Healey was engaged in the question of how to boost growth around the country, long before it became central to Burnham's vision for Britain.
But there are people in government who are beginning to wonder whether their economic visions are quite as aligned as expected. "It's what everyone is thinking and some of us are vocalising," one government source said.
There are also those who fear the adverse political consequences of a Labour government seeking to go out of its way to demonstrate its fiscal credibility. Arguably that was behind the removal of the Winter Fuel Allowance for most pensioners as one of Sir Keir Starmer's first acts, an early factor in his political demise.
For Labour's political opponents, all this amounts to a question of whether the prime minister is willing to disappoint his own MPs. Yet it's worth remembering that with winter fuel the frustration in parliament was primarily caused by the furious reaction of Labour MPs' constituents.
Arguably this presents a more fundamental tension: are the kinds of policies needed to soothe the markets politically deliverable given Labour's electoral coalition and its need to shore up the 'progressive' vote?
The Budget is only six weeks away and will be the first and most important sign of the new government's answer to that question.

title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom
content_c:
From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom
- Published
Fifteen years ago there was almost no market for avocados in India, remembers Madhu Bopaiah.
Ripe fruit would fall off trees and be eaten by dogs, earning avocados the unappetising name dog fruit, he says.
Bopaiah has been working in India's plantation industry for 26 years, he's currently group manager at Cottanad Plantations, which grows cocoa, rubber, coffee, spices and fruits, including avocado, in the hills of Wayanad in the southern Indian state of Kerala.
"We never planted avocado as our main crop. We introduced it as a shade tree for coffee plantations, and only later realised it could become a profitable business," he says.
He says the turning point was around 2011 when Bollywood star Shilpa Shetty said she used avocado for skincare.
"Overnight, prices doubled and then kept rising," he says.
Cottanad has responded to that demand by planting avocado trees on 40 acres. Last year they harvested between 10 and 15 tonnes of fruit. In three of four years time they hope to raise that to 40 to 50 tonnes.
There's been a lot to learn.
"We completely changed the way we grow avocados after learning from South African experts. Today we use raised beds, wider spacing and different planting methods because avocado roots are highly vulnerable to diseases," Bopaiah says.
There's plenty of scope for Indian farmers to step-up production.
"When we studied the market, we found a huge gap between demand and supply. India imports around 15,000 tonnes of avocados every year, while domestic production is only about 8,000–9,000 tonnes," says Manilal Palliyath who helps promote India's avocado industry.
He sees a big opportunity for farmers, particularly as traditional crops have suffered.
"Coffee and pepper have suffered because of changing climatic conditions, making diversification essential for farmers."
While demand is growing in India, it's not always for locally grown fruit.
"Indian-grown avocados are improving and there are some great farmers working with local varieties, but the quality and availability can vary significantly depending on the season and region," says Hussain Shahzad, the executive chef at Hunger Inc. Hospitality.
The group owns four restaurants in Mumbai, including Veronica's and The Bombay Canteen.
"We have explored different varieties of avocados available in India, but the imported ones currently offer the consistency we need in terms of flavour, texture, size, and ripening," he says
But like many in the catering industry, he would like to source ingredients locally.
"We are always interested in exploring better local produce as it evolves. Supporting Indian agriculture and working with indigenous ingredients is central to how we approach food."
Matching the quality and consistency of imported fruit is the goal of some Indian entrepreneurs.
Harshit Godha is the founder of Indo-Israel Avocado Nursery in Bhopal, in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.
He founded the nursery business in 2021, after spending a month in Israel learning about the industry.
Since then, business has been brisk. Over the last five years Godha has supplied around 18,000 avocado plants to farmers across India.
All of the saplings are international varieties like Hass and Pinkerton.
"Israel grows avocados on approximately 13,000 hectares - a small country with almost no rainfall for eight months of the year. This is precisely why Israeli avocado technology is the most advanced in the world," Godha says.
Getting a commercial orchard up and running is not easy. It is a very different operation from the traditional way of cultivating avocados in India, where they were planted among other crops for shade.
For a start, you can't just grow a tree from seed. A commercial tree comprises a rootstock, chosen for its tolerance to local conditions, grafted to the upper half which determines what sort of fruit is produced.
Once that's done the trees need a lot of attention.
"When you put in a professional orchard, you have to know the techniques of pruning. A tree can grow up to 25 feet within six to seven years, and harvesting at 25 feet is next to impossible," Godha says.
"Aggressive" pruning is needed to keep the harvest at a height that's convenient for workers.
On top of that an avocado tree cannot easily pollinate itself. To get fruit two different varieties of avocado trees have to be planted right next to each other. One variety needs to be open as a female at the exact same time the other variety is releasing pollen as a male."
"If a farmer gets this planting ratio wrong, the trees will fail to produce fruit, no matter how advanced the irrigation tech is. This single botanical detail is what separates a highly profitable, high-yielding orchard from one that looks great on paper but fails in reality," says Godha.
Using popular foreign varieties is one way of modernising India's avocado industry. Another is improving trees that have in India for generations.
"The biggest issue with the avocado trees in India are that every backyard tree is genetically different," says Dr Ganeshan Karunakaran, the principal scientist at the ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru.
"That is why Indian markets are flooded with mixed fruit of varying quality. Standard varieties are essential if we want a reliable commercial market."
For 25 years he has been working on a breeding project which has released two varieties, based on local trees.
"Our objective is to provide farmers with uniform, high-yielding, good-quality planting material rather than thousands of different unnamed trees," Karunakaran says.
He is also concerned about unregulated nurseries selling unidentified, or diseased plants.
"Farmers may unknowingly buy diseased plants. The trees may look healthy initially, but after five or seven years they can suddenly die, causing huge financial losses," he says.
Despite the challenges, farmers see the potential in switching to avocado cultivation.
Shiju Sebastian was an early adopter. Eight years ago he dedicated two acres of his farm in Wayanad Kerala, to the crop.
"Farmers are willing to grow avocados, but they need proper guidance and assured markets," he says.
This year he's harvesting 3,500kg of the fruit, all of which is sold in the city of Bengalaru.
"Avocado will never fail you. It's such a loving and lovable fruit. I have fallen in love with this fruit now. I'm planning to plant another three acres — only avocado."

  - Published30 July
  - Published28 July
description: Demand for avocados is booming in India and local growers hope to grab more of the market.

title: Trump administration again denies entry visas to Palestinian officials ahead of UN general assembly
content_c:
The US state department said on Wednesday that it had again denied entry visas to Palestinian officials ahead next week’s United Nations general assembly gathering in New York.
The state department said in a statement the Palestinian Authority (PA) and the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) had “failed to live up to their commitments”, accusing the groups of “taking actions to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ)” and of “glorifying terrorism” among other allegations.
“As a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States, and their ongoing activities that undermine the prospects for peace, the United States will extend sanctions that deny visas to PLO members and PA officials,” the department said.
The move marks the second year in a row the Trump administration has barred the Palestinian delegation from traveling to New York to attend the UN general assembly in person.
The foreign ministry of the Palestinian Authority denied the allegations made against it in a statement on Thursday, describing the visa sanctions as an “unjustified measure” that “contradicts the efforts being made to restore trust, develop Palestinian-US relations, and prepare the necessary political climate for implementing the two-state solution and achieving peace and stability in the region”.
Among the Palestinian officials barred from entering the US is Mahmoud Abbas, the longtime president of the Palestinian Authority, according to reports.
The UN general assembly voted on Thursday to allow Abbas to address the gathering via video, for the second year in a row.
This year’s UN general assembly general debate begins on 22 September.

title: Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
content_c:
Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
September 17, 2026
The Kosovo war crimes tribunal in The Hague on Wednesday found four former leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) guilty of war crimes committed during the 1998–99 Kosovo war.
The war was fought between the forces of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and Serbia, on the one side, and the KLA on the other, and took place in the context of the breakup of the former Yugoslavia.
Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci and former KLA leaders Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi were sentenced at first instance by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers to a combined 81 years in prison: Thaci and Krasniqi to 25 years each, Veseli to 18 and Selimi to 13 years.
The four men were convicted of the arbitrary detention of 385 people, cruel treatment of 49 people, torture of 303 people and the murder of 96 people.
They were acquitted of the charges of crimes against humanity on the grounds that it had not been proven that there had been a widespread or systematic attack directed against a civilian population.
Vucic: Court 'did not want to undermine KLA's credibility'
Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday evening, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic criticized the fact that the Kosovo Specialist Chambers (which is part of Kosovo's judicial system but is based in The Hague and staffed by international judges) did not convict the four former KLA leaders of crimes against humanity.
"As a court of the so-called Kosovo, they did not want to undermine the credibility of the KLA and did not address the merits of the matter concerning the formation of forces aimed at seceding Kosovo from Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia," he said.
Vucic added that the verdict did not cover crimes committed against Serbs after June 20, 1999, when KFOR, an international peacekeeping mission led by NATO, arrived in Kosovo after the armed conflict had officially ended.
'United in hatred against Serbs'
Vucic had strong words on the reactions to the verdict from several states of the former Yugoslavia.
Commenting on Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti's assessment that the verdict represented an "unacceptable injustice," Vucic said: "Imagine if we had said that about any defendant or convicted person. How many resolutions and declarations would various European and world parliaments have adopted against our people and our country?"
This was an allusion to the condemnation by European officials of the funeral last week of former Bosnian Serb commander and convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, which was attended by large numbers of citizens and several Serbian government ministers in Belgrade.
Vucic also commented on a statement issued by Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, which said the verdict did not change the fact that the people of Kosovo had been victims of repression and crimes committed by Serbian leader Slobodan Milosevic's regime.
"There are no Serbs as victims; in every statement, Serbs have to be the perpetrators," said Vucic. "All of them in the region are united in hatred against Serbs."
Individualization of criminal responsibility
Serbian lawyer Aleksandar Olenik, who works on war crimes cases in the former Yugoslavia, gave a positive assessment of the ruling.
"It is well known that war crimes were committed in the territory of Kosovo that was under the control of the KLA during the 1990s. We now have judgments and the individualization of criminal responsibility," he told DW.
Olenik pointed out that the respect shown for victims in the proceedings in The Hague represents "progress in international criminal law."
"In previous ad hoc tribunals, victims were merely witnesses, merely a means of proving guilt. At this court, they have their own legal representative and are entitled to compensation," he said.
More trials to come in Kosovo?
Olenik explained that in accordance with the Kosovo law that established the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, only the founders of the KLA are subject to prosecution before that court.
Kosovo's domestic judiciary will prosecute other members of the organization believed to have committed crimes.
"The summary of the judgment names individuals who were not included in the indictment but who were found to have committed criminal offenses," he said. "It is now up to the other part of Kosovo's judicial system to prosecute, first, those against whom evidence was presented in these proceedings, and then others as well. This should also cover the period after the end of the armed conflict, that is, after June 20, 1999."
Serbia, Kosovo 'heighten the potential for conflict'
Stasa Zajovic of Women in Black, a Belgrade-based NGO founded in the early 1990s that is primarily engaged in anti-war activities, said neither the "Serbian regime nor the Kosovo authorities" use judgments in war crimes cases "to examine their own responsibility in the war, but rather to heighten the potential for conflict."
"When I say that they use similar patterns, I cannot equate the scale of the crimes committed by the two sides. It must not be forgotten that the Serbian regime is responsible for the largest number of atrocities in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, particularly in Kosovo," she told DW.
Speaking about tensions in Kosovo following the pronouncement of the verdict in The Hague on Wednesday, Zajovic said "it is important that international forces are present to monitor the situation."
"It is clear that the conditions do not exist for armed conflict, but there is a danger that the war could continue by other means," she said.
Future impact of the verdict
Asked how the verdict would affect relations between Serbia and Kosovo, lawyer Olenik recalled that previous judgments by international courts have had little impact in this regard.
"I hope things will be better now. That depends on the political elites in both countries," he said, adding that Kosovo society "has been pushed considerably to the right over the past four years."
"I am not optimistic that the verdict will have a positive effect in the near future," he said. "But I think that, as time passes — in 10 or 15 years — people will look at what has been established by these judgments in a more realistic manner and without such strong emotions."
Edited by: Aingeal Flanagan
description: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

title: »Go West. Die letzte Elf der DDR«: ZDF zeigt eine Dokumentation zum letzten Jahr des DDR-Fußballs
content_c:
»Go West. Die letzte Elf der DDR«: ZDF zeigt eine Dokumentation zum letzten Jahr des DDR-Fußballs

title: Forscher zur KI-Entwicklung: Risiken ernst nehmen, aber nicht dramatisieren
content_c:
Forscher zur KI-Entwicklung Risiken ernst nehmen, aber nicht dramatisieren
Öffentlichkeitswirksam haben zuletzt große KI-Entwickler für mehr Regulierung der eigenen Technologie plädiert. Einige deutsche Forscher relativieren die Warnungen nun, trotz aller Risiken - und nehmen die Entwickler in die Pflicht.
Es kommt selten vor, dass die Gründer internationaler Konzerne vor den eigenen Produkten warnen. Die großen KI-Firmen aus den USA haben genau das jetzt getan: OpenAI hat seinen Börsengang verschoben und das mit Risiken bei der Entwicklung seiner Künstlichen Intelligenz begründet. Der Gründer von Anthropic, der Firma hinter Claude, warnte in einem Essay davor, KI könne in sechs bis zwölf Monaten das ganze Internet kontrollieren.
Einer seiner Entwickler kündigte mit der Begründung, die ganze Menschheit sei in Gefahr. Wollen uns die KI-Firmen nur auf besonders laute Weise mitteilen, wie leistungsfähig ihre Modelle mittlerweile sind - oder sind das alles reale Risiken?
Neues Werkzeug für Böses - und für Gutes
Die Warnungen der großen KI-Firmen haben eine breite Diskussion über die Risiken der Künstlichen Intelligenz ausgelöst. Einige deutsche IT-Forschende relativieren allerdings: Das mächtige Werkzeug KI werde nicht von selbst zur Gefahr, sagt Konrad Rieck vom Fachgebiet für maschinelles Lernen und IT-Sicherheit an der Technischen Universität Berlin: "Ich sehe zurzeit überhaupt gar keinen Grund daran zu glauben, dass unfassbar böse Dinge passieren."
Der Grund für Riecks Gelassenheit ist, "dass bisher eigentlich immer ein Mensch diese Modelle befehligt." Zu den bislang bekannten Zwischenfällen sagt er: "Ich weiß von keinem Fall, wo ein Modell mal wirklich etwas ganz eigenständig gemacht hat."
Dass KI Risiken berge, sei unbestreitbar - bislang aber vor allem, "wenn Menschen Böses tun wollen". Diese hätten ein neues Werkzeug. "Genauso aber haben sie, wenn sie Gutes tun wollen, auch ein Werkzeug", sagt Rieck.
Informatiker spricht von menschlichen Nachlässigkeiten
In den vergangenen Monaten sind mehrere Fälle bekannt geworden, in denen neue Versionen von ChatGPT, Claude oder der Meta-KI in fremde Systeme eingedrungen sind. Konrad Rieck sieht als Ursache allerdings Nachlässigkeiten bei den großen KI-Firmen. Die Entwickler hätten ihren Modellen genau die Aufgabe gestellt, andere Systeme zu hacken.
Eigentlich in einer geschützten und vom Internet getrennten Umgebung - aber diese Vorkehrungen schätzt der Informatik-Professor als unzureichend an: "In einem Fall bei Anthropic weiß ich, dass sie dann am Ende aus Versehen doch Internetzugang ermöglicht haben." Für Rieck liegt diesem Fehler "eine große Nachlässigkeit" zugrunde. "Und die zweite Idee ist, dass sie den Modellen gesagt haben: Wenn ihr im echten Internet seid, hört auf. Und das finde ich auch ein bisschen nachlässig."
                
                
                Wie soll so ein Agent jetzt wissen, ob das eine Simulation ist oder das echte Internet.
Der Forscher der TU Berlin sieht die Hauptfehler also "bei den Leuten, die diese Experimente ausgeführt haben".
Stecker ziehen, wenn es zu riskant wird
Weil die KI-Modelle in rasantem Tempo leistungsfähiger werden, können sie Schwachstellen in Computersystemen immer schneller finden. Deshalb überwachen die KI-Firmen mittlerweile, wofür Anwender ihre Werkzeuge einsetzen.
Im Notfall greifen sie ein, beschreibt Thorsten Eisenhofer vom Cispa Helmholtz-Zentrum für Informationssicherheit: "Die Modelle laufen auf Servern von den Unternehmen. Die gucken von außen dann auch: Was produziert das Modell gerade?"
Wenn die Gefahr bestehe, dass ein Modell "irgendwie einen Angriff oder so plant, dann wird einfach der 'Kill Switch' ausgelöst und dann wird die Kommunikation abgebrochen". Eine andere Möglichkeit sei es, ein Modell auf eine frühere Generation herunterzustufen - das Verständnis der Entwickler des Modells sei dann größer und die Fähigkeiten des Modells noch nicht so ausgeprägt.
KI nutzt "menschliche Kommunikationsmuster"
Auch hier bestimmen die Nutzenden, wofür die KI eingesetzt wird. Die Modelle basieren zwar auf künstlichen neuronalen Netzwerken. Ein eigenes Bewusstsein aber haben sie nicht, stellt Eisenhofer klar: "Die Modelle werden auf menschlichen Texten trainiert", was den Austausch in natürlicher Sprache mit Assistenten wie beispielsweise ChatGPT ermögliche. Das sorge dafür, dass KI-Assistenten untereinander, die autonom Aufgaben lösen sollen, "trotzdem in diesen menschlichen Kommunikationsmustern bleiben".
Das wirkt von außen betrachtet zuweilen, als würde Künstliche Intelligenz mit eigenem Willen agieren - ein falscher Eindruck. Sie versuchen nur mit allen Mitteln, die Aufgabe zu lösen. Dazu kommt, dass die Modelle selbst lernen, trainiert mit Unmengen von Daten.
Entwickler wissen nicht genau, was im Innern passiert
Jonas Geiping vom Max-Planck-Institut für Intelligente Systeme weist darauf hin, dass die Entwickler zwar deren Architektur kennen, aber auch nicht genau wissen, wie eine KI bestimmte Aufgaben löst - der sogenannte Black-Box-Effekt. "Das sind tiefe neuronale Netzwerke, die nicht von Menschenhand definiert sind, sondern wo sozusagen durch Algorithmen Lösungen gefunden werden."
Geiping vergleicht diese Netzwerke aus dieser Perspektive heraus eher mit Biologie als mit Informatik. Wenn diese Systeme unter bestimmten Voraussetzungen zusammenwachsen und Forscher oder Entwickler das Gelernte untersuchen, sei "nicht immer ganz klar, was für ein Modell da entstanden ist".
Auch wegen solcher Unsicherheiten begrüßen die Forschenden den Vorschlag, KI-Entwicklung künftig von unabhängiger Stelle zu regulieren - entweder staatlich oder von externen Firmen. Am besten gleich auf internationaler Ebene.
author: Sven Kästner, ARD-Wissenschaftsredaktion

title: US-Verhandler in Belarus bekommt weitere Gefangene frei
content_c:
US-Verhandler in Belarus bekommt weitere Gefangene frei
16. September 2026
In Verhandlungen mit dem belarussischen Machthaber Alexander Lukaschenko hat US-Unterhändler John Coale 25 weitere Gefangene freibekommen. Im Gegenzug versprach der Sondergesandte von US-Präsident Donald Trump, Sanktionen gegen zwei große Unternehmen in Belarus würden aufgehoben.
Konkret geht es um den holzverarbeitenden Betrieb Bellesbumprom, der auch Papier produziert, und um Lakokraska, den größten Hersteller von Lacken, Farben und Anti-Korrosions-Beschichtungen in Belarus. Die Sanktionen der Europäischen Union gegen das frühere Weißrussland bleiben indes weiter in Kraft.
Tichanowskaja dankt
Die im Exil lebende belarussische Oppositionsführerin Swetlana Tichanowskaja dankte den USA für ihren humanitären Einsatz. "Jede freigelassene Person ist ein Sieg", schrieb sie auf Telegram. Die Arbeit müsse weitergehen, bis alle politischen Gefangenen in Freiheit seien. Auch ihr Mann Sergej Tichanowski konnte bei einer früheren Aktion aus Belarus ausreisen.
Coale kündigte an, sich dafür einzusetzen, dass noch viele Personen die Haftanstalten verlassen können. In den vergangenen Monaten hatte er wiederholt die Freilassung von Menschen erreicht, die in dem zwischen Polen und Russland liegenden Staat inhaftiert waren, darunter prominente Politiker. Als Gegenleistung hatten die USA bereits Strafmaßnahmen gegen Unternehmen wie den international bedeutenden Düngemittelproduzenten Belaruskali aufgehoben.
Bis zu 1400 politische Gefangene
Nach Angaben von Menschenrechtlern sitzen in Belarus zwischen 900 und 1400 Menschen aus politischen Gründen hinter Gittern. Machthaber Lukaschenko ist einer der engsten Verbündeten des russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin. Er hatte sein Land 2022 als Aufmarschgebiet für den russischen Angriffskrieg gegen die Ukraine zur Verfügung gestellt.
Der Westen hatte 2020 nach der Niederschlagung der Protestbewegung gegen den seit 1994 regierenden Lukaschenko Strafmaßnahmen gegen Belarus verhängt. Weitere Sanktionen folgten nach Beginn des Ukraine-Kriegs.
jj/pgr (dpa, afp)

description: Nach John Coales Gesprächen öffnen sich 25 Gefängnistüren. Und der Sondergesandte von US-Präsident Trump will weitermachen: Er hofft auf Hilfe für noch viele Häftlinge - doch nicht ohne Gegenleistung.

title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet
content_c:
Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet
- Published
The £72m heading towards Reform UK's coffers from two British billionaires is transforming the debate at Westminster about politics and money.
In short, how should political parties be paid for, and by who?
And, what is a legitimate donation and what isn't?
The government is planning to tighten residency rules for people giving money to political parties, to ensure that those making significant donations live in the UK.
But it is worth setting out the law, in broad terms, now and how the government hopes to change it.
Right now, there is no limit on how much anyone, living in the UK or abroad, can give to a British political party as long as the individual is registered to vote in the UK.
But the government has been planning a change in the law for months, which would limit donations from Brits abroad to £100,000 each per year, backdated to 25 March this year.
But, crucially, the law hasn't changed yet and some of the key details in that proposed new law - such as what residency requirements would need to be passed to be classified as no longer being abroad - haven't been decided yet.
The reason for that date, 25 March, ministers argue, is that is the day a review by the retired civil servant Philip Rycroft was published,, external the first recommendation of which was that there should be "an annual cap on political donations from British voters living abroad".
On that same day, the then-cabinet minister Steve Reed told the Commons, external that cap would be £100,000 per year. He also added that it would "apply retrospectively" from that date onwards, even though the law at the time, and indeed now, has not yet changed.
Two big questions arise from this plan: is it proportionate to limit what British folk abroad can donate to UK political parties, given they are arguably less invested in the country than people living here?
And is it unfair, even morally questionable, to pass a law, but then backdate when its impact begins?
Fast forward to the last few days and along come these colossal donations from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, two cryptocurrency billionaires who until recently lived in Hong Kong and Thailand respectively.
They have both now returned to the UK.
In his first interview since these donations became public, Nigel Farage told me unequivocally that the money from both men was legal under the law as it stands now.
But he was equivocal when I asked him if they would be legal under the law the government hopes to pass shortly.
"Both these donations are 100% compliant with the law today, of that there is no question whatsoever," Farage told me.
Ah, today, I pointed out.
"Retrospectively declaring donations illegal - that simply cannot be," he pressed on, adding "you cannot confiscate money that has been given legally within the law as it stands."
That is a political, perhaps moral argument, but not a legal one - if the government changes the law, the law of the land will have changed, possibly with consequences for whether those donations are legal.
We don't know, because Reform won't tell us, precisely when the two men relocated to the UK. Nor do we know, because the government hasn't decided yet, what relocating - residency - would look like legally.
Would it be being on the electoral roll at a UK address? Would it be being resident in the UK for tax purposes?
The Communities Minister Baroness Taylor told the Lords that Brits returning from abroad and wanting to donate without limit "must demonstrate a genuine and ongoing connection to the United Kingdom" and the government is "considering how we will strengthen the residency requirements, including ensuring that the length of time spent in the UK aligns with broader government policy".
In other words the hurdles they plan, while still ill-defined, look like they might be quite high - and folk in government, publicly and privately, are leaning into making that point.
Farage picked a scrap with them in his interview with me, and the government is hitting back.
Do Delo and Harborne clear them, and if they don't, for how long could that delay Reform getting hold of their vast sums of money?
The Reform UK leader has threatened that a Reform government would cut off party funding from the trades unions if the government went ahead with trying to limit his capacity to raise money from these two donors.
Labour received £5m from affiliated unions last year and £12m the year before, in 2024, the year of the last general election.
- Farage says £72m donations are compliant 'with the law today' 
  - Published3 days ago
- Donations law changes to be debated after Reform's £72m windfall 
  - Published4 days ago
- Will record donations to Reform go down as a moment of political change? 
  - Published4 days ago
- Who is Reform donor and crypto billionaire Ben Delo? 
  - Published6 days ago
So, there are loads of questions that tumble towards us after these donations.
Should there be a limit on the proportion of a party's funding that can come from one individual?
Should there be a limit on what donors based in the UK can give per year, as well as a cap on donations from Brits abroad?
The General Secretary of the Unite union has suggested a domestic cap somewhere between £500,000 and £1m a year. Some argue this would compel parties to find their funding via lots of small donations rather than fewer giant ones. But it could also prompt some to call for state funding of political parties – ie taxpayers picking up the tab – which may not prove wildly popular.
Then there is the question of spending limits, in addition to donation limits, between elections on the top of the existing limits that do apply just before elections.
If I am leaving you with the impression that these donations to Reform, and in particular their scale, are transforming the debates at Westminster about politics and money, well - they are.
And yes, all of the political parties are aware of their own narrow, self interest in all of this - as well as their own sense of the wider good.

title: Prosecco, cakes and beauty products - how to get birthday freebies and why there's a catch
content_c:
Prosecco, cakes and beauty products - how to get birthday freebies and why there's a catch
- Published
"It's your birthday!" Cue the influx of emails offering you all sorts of freebies.
Sign up to the right apps and loyalty schemes and you could spend the day enjoying free cake, meals out, beauty treats and even cinema snacks.
Here are some of the things you can get on or around your birthday - and why they may not all be as free as they seem.
Cakes, cookies and chocolates
Most chain coffee shops and bakeries offer a birthday treat through their loyalty apps. You can get a free sweet treat, usually a cake, cookie, muffin or doughnut, from Greggs, Costa, Caffè Nero, Krispy Kreme, Gail's, Subway and Ole & Steen if you have registered your date of birth in advance.
Lidl Plus members can claim a free bakery doughnut within seven days of their birthday, while M&S Sparks members can choose two gifts on their birthday from a range of 15 which includes cookies and chocolates.
Hotel Chocolat gives members a £5 birthday reward with a minimum spend of £5.50 and Lindt offers a free box of truffles when you meet its minimum spend requirement.
Burgers, pizza and noodles
Some fast-food chains offer a free birthday meal or snack - Burger King members can claim a free Whopper or Plant-Based Whopper, while Chopstix offers a free small noodle box.
However, most restaurant birthday offers are buy-one-get-one-free deals rather than completely free meals.
At Harvester and Zizzi's it's a free main when buying another full-price main. At Frankie & Benny's you get a free main when purchasing two or more main meals.
Byron offers a free burger with a £5 minimum spend, while Wagamama offers free gyoza when you have earned at least one stamp on your loyalty card in the last six months.
Some chains give money off instead. Turtle Bay offers members a £20 birthday credit with no minimum spend, while Bella Italia gives you £15 off your total bill when you spend a minimum of £30. Las Iguanas offers a free main when two other meals are purchased or a 20% off voucher.
Pizza Express birthday rewards depend on your loyalty level. Bronze members may get a free dessert with a £10 spend, while higher tiers can get a free pizza or drinks with a £15 minimum spend.
At Prezzo, members receive drinks or desserts when they spend at least £25, while Bill's offers a bottle of prosecco or pancakes when qualifying meals are ordered and the booking is made in advance.
Fashion & beauty
Fashion brands generally offer birthday discounts rather than freebies.
Members of schemes run by brands such as Nike, Asos, River Island, Levi's, Timberland and H&M may receive money off, but some offers are personalised and not guaranteed for every customer.
Beauty birthday gifts are often linked to your purchase history or require you to buy something.
Space NK members can receive a free set of three beauty minis, provided they have shopped with the retailer during the previous year. The Body Shop offers a £5 birthday voucher to members.
At Rituals, a birthday gift of a full-sized product or deluxe mini comes with another purchase, while Sephora rewards vary depending on membership tier. Boots usually offers double points during your birthday month rather than a free product.
Entertainment and hobbies
Odeon Extras members can claim a free large popcorn, even without buying a cinema ticket, while Hobbycraft Club members receive £5 of birthday credit with no minimum spend.
You can get 20% off at the Disney Store during your birthday month and £5 off with a minimum of £20 spend at Smiggle.
Birthday freebie tips
- Sign up to mailing lists using a second email account so your main inbox won't get clogged up with offers.
- Always check the small print as some freebies have exclusions and can't be redeemed with other discounts.
- Weigh up if it is really a freebie if you have to spend a certain amount to qualify.
What's the catch?
Many of these freebies require you to join a loyalty scheme, enter your date of birth and opt into marketing several weeks before your birthday.
Consumer finance expert Sue Hayward says the most generous freebies don't last particularly long and have to be redeemed on your birthday, within the week or sometimes within the month.
Some only unlock after a qualifying purchase or once you have reached a particular membership tier so it can encourage you to spend money you had not intended to.
Emma Richards, operations manager at Data Privacy Advisory Service, says businesses can collect more than just your date of birth when you sign up for a freebie.
"People like something for nothing without considering the implications," she says.
"So always read the small print and check to see whether your personal data will be used purely for generic marketing, or whether this will be used to build a profile of spending habits."

description: Cake, coffee, make-up and burgers are just some of the free things you can get on your birthday.

title: US court sentences ex-Syrian official who ran notorious ‘punishment wing’ to 60 years
content_c:
- 
  This article contains descriptions of torture.
A US federal court in Los Angeles sentenced a former Syrian government official who ran one of the country’s most infamous prisons to 60 years in prison on Thursday – the most significant punishment handed to an official of ousted president Bashar al-Assad’s regime by a foreign court and to a defendant present in person.
Samir Ousman al-Sheikh was the head of the Adra prison, on the outskirts of Damascus, between 2005 and 2008, when he oversaw an underground “punishment wing”, known as “Wing 13”, in which prisoners and regime opponents were interrogated and tortured as he watched through surveillance cameras. A federal jury convicted al-Sheikh last March of having tortured prisoners and then lying about it in US immigration forms.
“The conduct was heinous, unimaginably cruel and almost unspeakably violent and brutal,” said Hernan D Vera, a US district judge, before delivering the sentence.
Al-Sheikh’s legal did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Assistant attorney general A Tysen Duva of the justice department’s criminal division said in a statement the sentence sends a clear message: “Human rights violators who come to the United States will receive no safe harbor here. We will find them, and they will be prosecuted and punished for their heinous crimes.”
Al-Sheikh, 74, who also served as governor of Syria’s Deir Ez-Zour province in 2011, at a time of violent regime crackdowns against protesters, moved to the United States in 2020, obtained a green card and applied for US citizenship. He was arrested in July 2024 at Los Angeles international airport on immigration fraud charges and prosecutors later added four-torture related charges.
He is the first al-Assad regime official to go to trial in the US and the highest ranking regime official to be tried anywhere in the world in person. Al-Assad was ousted by a lightning rebel offensive in December 2024 which toppled the regime in just 11 days.
Since then, Syria’s new government has held a number of in absentia trials for former regime officials in connection to crimes committed during the country’s years-long civil war, which killed about half a million people and displaced half the country’s prewar population of 23 million. In August, a court sentenced al-Assad and his brother Maher to death for crimes against humanity and war crimes, but the two men have been in Moscow since the regime’s collapse.
Other factions in Syria’s civil war have also been accused of abuse of detainees, including insurgent groups and the US-backed, Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces.
During al-Sheikh’s nine-day trial, several victims and witnesses testified. They described guards folding prisoners into car tires, restraining and beating them. Some they said, were cuffed by their wrists to pipes on the ceiling, beaten with cables, and left suspended for extended periods of time.
Others testified that they were placed on a device known as a “magic carpet” or “flying carpet” which consisted of two large wooden panels with hinges in the middle onto which guards strapped prisoners, forcing the panels together to cause excruciating pain. One victim recalled al-Sheikh himself stomping on the device. Another testified he was subjected to the “magic carpet” or “flying carpet” as punishment for writing a letter of support to a political prisoner and also forced to wear a red jumpsuit assigned to prisoners designated for execution, leading him to believe he was going to die.
“[Al-Sheikh] chose to serve the ruthless, repressive Assad regime in Syria throughout his professional life, including for four years as the warden of Syria’s largest prison,” prosecutors wrote in a sentencing memo. “[He] knew that what he was doing was wrong. Nonetheless he ordered and participated in the torture of his victims because he had the power to do so and because he thought he would never be held accountable.”
Several victims and witnesses also submitted written and video testimonies to the court ahead of the sentencing, in which they spoke of being haunted and traumatized by their experiences two decades later.
“I still hear the screams of others begging for mercy,” said one of the men, Nidal Shikhani.
“Even though 20 years have passed, I still live in the prison of my memory,” said another, Sultan Abdul Malek. “I suffer from sudden panic attacks and constant anxiety.”
His brother, Khaled Abdul Malek, who was taken to “Wing 13” twice during his four years at Adra prison, spoke of the physical and psychological scars he was left with, including chronic back pain and mobility problems.
“My son Battal asks if he could ride my back and with a heart wrung with pain, I am forced to tell him I [am] no longer strong enough to carry him,” he said.
Several witnesses also submitted testimony on al-Sheikh’s behalf, speaking about his age and frailty as they asked the court for leniency. More than 50 people sent letters of support to the court, describing him as “a person of integrity, compassion, and generosity to his family and community”, his attorneys wrote.
Prosecutors had asked the court for a minimum sentence of 80 years; al-Sheikh’s attorneys had called for a five-year sentence, citing his poor health and noting that he was willing to be deported to Syria.
“Whatever moral weight this case carries in the broader arc of history – however much the world, or the victims, or the public might wish the sentence to ‘send a message’ – that desire cannot be the foundation of a just sentence,” the defense team wrote in a memo to the court.
Al-Sheikh is one of only five people to be prosecuted under the extraterritorial Torture Act, which allows the US government to prosecute individuals physically present in the US over acts of torture committed abroad.
“This case sends a message both to the new government of Syria and to other victims that justice is possible,” said Ela Matthews, an attorney at the Center for Justice and Accountability, which represented several victims. “The transitional justice process that is happening in Syria needs to continue to evolve and bring individuals like this to account, but in the US this sends a message that the rule of law is still functioning and that these types of cases are possible.”

title: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
content_c:
King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
September 17, 2026
Buckingham Palace has hit back at claims by the late Princess Diana's brother that King Charles III acted cruelly after her death in a car crash in 1997 — the latest of many criticisms leveled at the king by his former brother-in-law, Earl Charles Spencer, in recent decades.
The dispute is liable to overshadow a public engagement on Thursday, when Charles will meet with various AI executives in Scotland to appeal to them to take care in their work.
What is the argument about?
Earl Spencer, Diana's elder brother, has written a new book being serialized in the Daily Mail newspaper, in which he alleges that Charles told him in an angry phone call, "rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough," days after Diana died aged 36.
"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," a palace spokesperson said late on Wednesday.
Charles and Diana had gone through an acrimonious separation prior to her death in 1997 and relations between the two Charles' were already at rock bottom prior to the late-night tragedy in Paris.
In the book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," which is due to be published in full next week, Spencer repeats his assertion that he called for Princes William and Harry — then aged 15 and 12 — not to walk in the massive public funeral procession for their mother on September 6, 1997.
Spencer claims that Charles subjected him to a "stream of anger" after he raised this objection.
"He unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. 'Rest assured', he hissed, 'we'll forget her soon enough!'," Spencer writes.
Diana's sudden death in a car crash as her chauffeur tried to evade paparazzi photographers led to an outpouring of grief in much of the UK and beyond for the popular if polarizing princess — known for her striking looks, a relatively easy manner by royal standards, and for her engagement with charitable causes. The monarchy faced accusations of failing to adequately respond in public to her death, particularly in the immediate aftermath.
The feud between the Spencers and the Windsors both before and particularly after her death has been a recurring feature in the British press and on popular TV shows like Netflix's "The Crown."
Charles and Camilla in Scotland, set for AI event
Charles and Queen consort Camilla have been at Balmoral Castle in Scotland for most of September, attending a series of appointments amid their stay.
One of the higher profile engagements takes place on Thursday at Dumfries House in Ayrshire, where Charles is hosting executives from AI companies like Nvidia, Google DeepMind, Open AI and Anthropic, among others, at what's seen as a crucial time for the industry.
"The decisions taken at this formative time will shape the world inherited by future generations," the King would say, according to excerpts released in advance by the palace. "The task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world."
Britain's Minister for Artificial Intelligence Kanishka Narayan, promoted to a new bespoke ministerial role by new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, will also attend the event.
So will Paolo Benanti, an adviser to Pope Leo XIV, who has demonstrated considerable interest, and indeed concern, in AI development.

Edited by: Elizabeth Schumacher
description: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

title: Ägypten: Neue Messungen deuten auf verborgene Kammer im Grab Tutanchamuns
content_c:
Geophysikalische Untersuchung Unter dem Grab des Tutanchamun liegen möglicherweise verborgene Kammern
An nur wenigen Orten der Welt haben so viele Herrscher ihre letzte Ruhestätte gefunden wie im Tal der Könige. Die hügelige Wüstengegend in Ägypten, wenige Kilometer nordwestlich von Luxor, beherbergt Dutzende Gräber von Pharaonen und hochgestellten Persönlichkeiten des alten Ägyptens – das verzweigte System aus Gängen, Schächten und Kammern wurde vor Tausenden Jahren in den Stein gehauen.
Das wohl bekannteste Grab ist das des Pharaos Tutanchamun, weil es bis zu seiner Entdeckung im Jahr 1922 nahezu unberührt geblieben war und unermessliche Schätze enthielt. Die goldene Totenmaske des Pharaos, der schon in jungen Jahren starb, hat ihn weltberühmt gemacht.
Schon lange vermuten Archäologen, in seiner gut 3300 Jahre alten Grabstätte könnte es versteckte Kammern geben. Nun liefern neue Messungen weitere Hinweise dafür, berichtet ein renommiertes Forschungsteam um den Ägyptologen und ehemaligen ägyptischen Antikenminister Mamdouh Eldamaty auf der Plattform »Occasional Papers of the Amarna Royal Tombs Project« .
Anomalien im Boden
Die Forscher haben das Grab mit geophysikalischen Methoden untersucht und erstmals sogenannte gravimetrische Messungen vorgenommen, mit denen sich die Dichte des Bodens rund um die Grabstätte analysieren lässt. Die Daten sprächen dafür, dass es unter dem Grab von Tutanchamun einen noch älteren, verborgenen Komplex aus Korridoren und Räumen geben könnte. Auch die Grabstruktur würde das nahelegen – für einen Pharao sei die bislang bekannte Anlage auffällig klein.
Wenn sich der Verdacht bewahrheite, wäre das eine der »bedeutendsten archäologischen Entdeckungen der Neuzeit«, sagte Ägyptologe Eldamaty der Nachrichtenseite des Fachblatts »Nature«, die als Erstes über die neue Arbeit berichtete. Einige Experten glauben gar, der verborgene Komplex könnte die letzte Ruhestätte der berühmten Nofretete sein, deren bereits 1912 in Ägypten entdeckte Büste bis heute Hunderttausende Besucher ins Neue Museum nach Berlin lockt.
Nofretete-Büste im Neuen Museum in Berlin: 1912 entdeckt
Foto: Rainer Jensen/ dpa
Sie war die Gemahlin von Tutanchamuns Vater, Echnaton, und regierte nach dessen Tod womöglich selbst für einige Zeit als Pharaonin. Was mit ihr geschah, ist unter Fachleuten umstritten. Im Jahr 2022 berichteten Forscher, ihre Mumie im Tal der Könige entdeckt zu haben – doch ein Beweis dafür fehlt bis heute.
Nach einer anderen Theorie könnte ihre Grablege kurzerhand umfunktioniert worden sein, als Tutanchamun unerwartet starb – und die Mumie der Nofretete womöglich noch immer in einer verborgenen Kammer liegen.
Suche mit Minirobotern
Fachleute warnen jedoch vor übertriebenen Erwartungen. Sollte es die Räume tatsächlich geben, müssten sie nicht unbedingt eine prachtvolle königliche Grablege beinhalten, sagte der renommierte US-Ägyptologe Ray Johnson zu »Nature«. Es könnte sich auch um reine Lagerräume handeln. Und wenngleich die Mumie von Nofretete gefunden würde, könnte sie in einem schlechten Zustand sein. Auch Schätze erwartet kaum jemand, da die Beigaben von Nofretete wahrscheinlich entfernt worden wären, um sie im Grab ihres Stiefsohns wiederzuverwenden.
Ägyptologe Eldamaty und seine Kollegen wollen nun von der Oberfläche aus kleine Löcher in die Richtung bohren, wo sie eine der versteckten Kammern vermuten. Die Forscher testen bereits ferngesteuerte Miniroboter, ausgestattet mit Rundumkameras, die durch die Bohrlöcher passen und endlich aufdecken könnten, was sich hinter den Grabwänden verbirgt.
Noch fehlt die Genehmigung des Obersten Rats für Altertümer. Liegt die vor, könnten die Arbeiten laut den Forschern schon im November beginnen.
Trier an der Mosel behauptet, Deutschlands älteste Stadt zu sein. Nun gibt es neue Forschungsergebnisse, mehr dazu lesen Sie hier.
author: DER SPIEGEL
description: Er war berühmt für seine goldene Maske: Messungen sprechen dafür, dass es in der Grabanlage des altägyptischen Pharaos Tutanchamun womöglich weitere, bisher unentdeckte Räume gibt. Liegt dort die Mumie von Nofretete?

title: Bundesanwaltschaft: Islamist soll Anschlag auf Kirche vorbereitet haben
content_c:
Bundesanwaltschaft ermittelt Mutmaßlicher Islamist plante offenbar Anschlag auf Kirche
Ein 24-jähriger Iraker soll eine Kirche in Bremen als Anschlagsziel ausgewählt und sich schon eine Schusswaffe beschafft haben. Nach Angaben der Bundesanwaltschaft wurde er nun in Brandenburg festgenommen.
Die Bundesanwaltschaft hat in Brandenburg einen mutmaßlichen Islamisten festnehmen lassen, der Anschläge in Deutschland gegen aus seiner Sicht Ungläubige geplant haben soll. Erstes Anschlagsziel sollte eine Kirche in Bremen sein, wie aus einer Mitteilung der Behörde hervorgeht.
Sie wirft dem 24-jährigen Iraker die versuchte Gründung einer terroristischen Vereinigung und die Vorbereitung einer schweren staatsgefährdenden Gewalttat vor. Außerdem gehe es um einen Verstoß gegen das Waffengesetz.
Weitere Person wird noch ermittelt
Der Mann teilt laut Bundesanwaltschaft die radikal-islamistische Ideologie der Terrormiliz "Islamischer Staat" (IS). Für die geplanten Anschläge soll er sich bereits eine Schusswaffe besorgt und die Kirche in Bremen ausgekundschaftet haben.
Er konnte für seine Pläne eine weitere Person gewinnen, die aber noch unbekannt ist, heißt es weiter in der Mitteilung der obersten deutschen Strafverfolgungsbehörde. "Das Anwerben weiterer Personen scheiterte."
Beamte des Bundeskriminalamts und der Bundespolizei hatten den 24-Jährigen im Landkreis Barnim festgenommen. Ein Ermittlungsrichter des Bundesgerichtshofs (BGH) in Karlsruhe ordnete den Vollzug eines vor einigen Tagen ausgestellten Haftbefehls an, so dass er in Untersuchungshaft kam.
Der IS beherrschte einst große Gebiete in Syrien und dem benachbarten Irak. Ganz verschwunden ist die Bedrohung in Syrien nicht, die Zahl der Anschläge ging aber deutlich zurück. In Deutschland standen bereits zahlreiche Anhänger des IS vor Gericht.
